basis: Genetically caused bone necrosis; metabolic and vascular mechanisms vary across subtypes.
Inherited corneal endothelial degeneration causing corneal dysfunction.
Epithelial neoplasm arising in the rectum.
Inherited retinal cone and rod degeneration with progressive visual impairment.
Developmental learning disorder impairing written language; neurodevelopmental disorders fall within neurologic.
GPI-anchor disorder with ID and phalangeal defects; sensorineural hearing loss 2/3. Rectal anomalies 4/7 omitted by cap; nail/globe changes lack proven functional damage.
Congenital unilateral fusion of the humerus and radius.
Acute injury of the macular retina causing persistent scotomas; retinal location belongs to ocular.
Lysosomal storage disease causing neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss occur in nearly all. Significant cardiac disease is age-dependent and less certain.
Proximal tubular bicarbonate wasting causes metabolic acidosis. Reduced bone density is described, but prevalence sufficient for the 30% threshold is not established.
Skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration define DMD; cognitive/learning impairment is very frequent (80-99% HPO). Ventilatory failure reflects muscle weakness, not direct lung injury.
Most mucoepidermoid carcinomas arise in major or minor salivary glands. Other primary sites are uncommon subtypes, not commonly involved organs.
Tumor of parasympathetic paraganglia at the skull base and middle ear; neural origin and middle-ear occupation define its location.
Infectious abscess of breast tissue; infection supplies a mechanism axis although breast itself has no anatomical axis.
Urinary bladder stone; the renal axis includes the lower urinary tract.
Defined by cerebellar hypoplasia and abnormal neurologic development and locomotion.
Primary podocyte injury with glomerular scarring. Proposed circulating permeability factors do not establish a definite immune mechanism.
Abnormal transthyretin binding alters measured thyroid hormone concentrations despite euthyroidism; no intrinsic thyroid or liver damage is implied.
Inherited leucine catabolism defect; most screening-detected patients are asymptomatic. Severe neurologic findings in selected case reports do not establish 30% prevalence.
Urogenital adysplasia denotes congenital urinary tract absence or dysplasia; associated reproductive abnormalities have no axis. Clinical detail is limited.
Glioneuronal neoplasm arising in the central nervous system, usually near the fourth ventricle.
Intellectual disability and pituitary hormone deficiency are defining components.
Persistent traumatic brain damage with cognitive decline and other neurologic dysfunction.
Pulmonary arterial disease with right-heart dysfunction; reduced DLCO reflects vascular dysfunction. Isolated stroke reports do not establish common neurologic injury.
Teratoma arises in the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes. Thyroid tissue content alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
